title: Foreign ownership rules out NTT Data Spain despite Spain's strongest private-sector bench
content:
The former everis, now NTT Data Spain, is credited with the strongest private-sector bench in Spain and a real OutSystems practice active across Spain, the UK, Portugal, Belgium and Italy, alongside Microsoft and SAP. The screen still rules it out, on ownership: it is foreign-owned.

Two criteria stack here, and it is worth separating them. The OutSystems practice is slot occupancy — the same disqualifier that demoted IG&H and ITSector, since a proprietary app-layer platform leaves no gap to fill. Foreign ownership is the one the note actually leads with, and it recurs across the corpus: the Japanese ownership of KMD and the absorption of Truewind into a French infrastructure group are recorded the same way.

The reason ownership is load-bearing rather than cosmetic is that the thesis being sold is sovereignty — client-owned infrastructure, local-first deployment, European procurement. A partner whose own decisions route through a parent outside the region is a weaker carrier of that argument, whatever the quality of its bench. Delivery strength does not compensate, which is why the strongest private-sector bench in the country sits at priority 9.
